title: Committee of Supply – Head L (Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head L (Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment)

sections.label: Low-carbon transition and zero-waste steps
sections.summary: Singapore is raising its carbon tax, tracking public sector sustainability, enhancing the Energy Efficiency Fund, and taking steps toward a zero-waste nation while extending the PWM to waste sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At home, we are transiting to a low-carbon future by raising the carbon tax to $25 per tonne, tracking the public sector's performance on sustainability through the GreenGov.SG Report and enhancing the Energy Efficiency Fund (E2F).

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We have also taken concrete steps towards becoming a zero-waste nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We introduced the disposable bag charge, the food waste reporting framework and will introduce the beverage container return scheme soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We are taking care of our lower-income workers by extending the PWM to the waste collection and materials recovery sectors.

sections.label: Shorter-term sustainability targets
sections.summary: Some targets are shorter-term, including quadrupling solar energy deployment by 2025 and developing over 130 hectares of new parks by 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Some of these targets are shorter-term, such as the plans to quadruple solar energy deployment by 2025 and to develop over 130 hectares of new parks by 2026.

sections.label: Planting trees and urban greenery
sections.summary: The first target is to plant one million more trees, enhance urban greenery and promote biodiversity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First one is to plant one million more trees, enhance our urban greenery as well as promoting biodiversity.

sections.label: Quadrupling solar energy deployment
sections.summary: Target number two is to quadruple solar energy deployment by 2025, accelerating the adoption of renewable energy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Target number two is to quadruple solar energy deployment by 2025, accelerating the adoption of renewable energy.

sections.label: Reducing waste sent to landfill
sections.summary: Number three is the reduction of waste sent to landfill by 30% by 2030, focusing on waste reduction and recycling.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Number three is the reduction of waste sent to landfill by 30% by 2030, focusing on waste reduction as well as recycling.

sections.label: Cleaner energy cars from 2030
sections.summary: Target number five is to ensure that all newly-registered cars are cleaner energy models from 2030 onwards, transiting to green transport.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Target number five is to ensure that all newly-registered cars are cleaner energy models from 2030 onwards, transiting to green transport.

sections.label: Rising sea levels and rainfall
sections.summary: The passage asks about rising sea levels and notes reported 2023 rainfall and temperature figures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Today, I want to ask about rising sea levels, as our coasts are vulnerable to floods and erosion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It was recently reported that Singapore's annual total rainfall was 13.1% above the long-term average in 2023 and the mean temperature for the last decade reached a new high of 28.06.

sections.label: Open ocean aquaculture licences
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Government safeguards natural habitats around open ocean aquaculture and what checks apply to new licences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How does the Government intend to safeguard natural habitats around open ocean aquaculture Bills, and what processes or checks are there when issuing new licences?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It has also been reported that 70 farms in Lim Chu Kang have had to move out for developmental purposes.

sections.label: Thai rice price and wet markets
sections.summary: The passage notes a record Thai rice price and asks about recognising wet market stallholders selling Singapore-grown produce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Thai 5% broken rice reached US$660 per metric tonne in end-January 2024, a record high.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can the Government consider giving recognition to wet market stallholders who supply Singapore-grown produce in the heartlands, including potential incentives, such as rental subsidies?

sections.label: Lim Chu Kang Agri-Food Hub
sections.summary: The passage states the Lim Chu Kang Agri-Food Production Hub is positioned as a key initiative supporting the "30 by 30" ambition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Lim Chu Kang Agri-Food Production Hub has been positioned as a key initiative to support Singapore's "30 by 30" ambition.

sections.label: 30 by 30 food goal
sections.summary: The passage states the Government's goal of producing 30% of Singapore's nutritional needs by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: The Government has set the goal of producing 30% of Singapore's nutritional needs by 2030.

sections.label: Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for an update on the $60 million Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Could the Minister provide an update on the $60 million Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund?

sections.label: Cultivated meat operations paused
sections.summary: The passage asks how Eat Just pausing Singapore operations affects the "30 by 30" food security goals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Lastly, given the announcement today by cultivated meat producer, Eat Just, that operations in Singapore will be paused, can the Minister shed light on how will this latest development affect Singapore's "30 by 30" food security goals?

sections.label: Singapore electricity from natural gas
sections.summary: The passage states that over 90% of Singapore's electricity is generated from natural gas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, over 90% of our electricity is generated from natural gas.

sections.label: Sustainability criteria in public tenders
sections.summary: The passage asks the timeline to expand sustainability criteria to more public sector procurement sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Last year, the Government announced that it would set aside up to 5% of evaluation points for environmental sustainability in public sector tenders, starting with large construction and ICT projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The reason for these two sectors is because, together, they make up more than 60% of the value of Government procurement contracts awarded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What is the timeline to expand the adoption of these sustainability criteria to more public sector procurement sectors?

sections.label: Singapore GHG emissions peak
sections.summary: The passage asks when Singapore's greenhouse gas emissions are expected to peak.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: When do we expect GHGs for Singapore to peak, so that efforts can be further focused on reduction towards net-zero?

sections.label: Scope 3 emissions disclosure
sections.summary: The passage asks whether disclosure will begin to include Scope 3 emissions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Will the disclosure begin to include Scope 3 emissions, as that is a critical aspect of the products or services procured?

sections.label: Future Energy Fund and SME funds
sections.summary: The passage notes the $5 billion Future Energy Fund and extended funds for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The $5 billion Future Energy Fund is a huge boost for the transition to cleaner fuels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I am also heartened by the extension and expansion of funds by SMEs, including through the Enterprise Financing Scheme and the Energy Efficiency Grant.

sections.label: Singapore carbon tax increase
sections.summary: Singapore's carbon tax rose from $5 to $25 per tonne, and will rise to $45 per tonne between 2026 and 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Chairman, as part of Singapore's efforts to mitigate climate change, our carbon tax was increased from the previous $5 per tonne of emissions to $25 per tonne.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It will rise to $45 per tonne between 2026 and 2027.

sections.label: Household switch water savings
sections.summary: If all eligible households switch, it equals taking 10,000 cars off the road and saves 400 million gallons of water annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: If all eligible households make the switch, this is the equivalent of taking 10,000 cars off the road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The water savings amount to 400 million gallons of water annually.

sections.label: Zero Waste Masterplan targets
sections.summary: Singapore's Zero Waste Masterplan aims to raise national recycling to 70% and cut landfill waste by 30% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Singapore's Zero Waste Masterplan aims to increase the overall national recycling rate to 70% and reduce waste sent to the landfill by 30% by 2030.

sections.label: Domestic recycling rate gap
sections.summary: Over half of Singaporean households said they recycled, but the actual domestic recycling rate was only 13%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Even though more than half of Singaporean households said they were recycling, the actual domestic recycling rate based on recyclables collected was only 13%.

sections.label: Deaths and afterlife arrangements
sections.summary: Deaths rose from 20,933 in 2020 to 25,600 in 2022, prompting a question on MSE's long-term strategy for afterlife arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: From 20,933 deaths in 2020, the number grew to 25,600 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What is MSE's long-term strategy and innovations, given that competing land needs and climate change concerns are rendering traditional ways of afterlife arrangements increasingly difficult?

sections.label: Hawker stall median rents
sections.summary: As of 2021, median monthly rent was $1,250 for non-subsidised NEA hawker stalls and $2,000 for privately-operated ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: As of 2021, the median monthly rent was $1,250 for non-subsidised stalls in NEA-operated hawker centres and $2,000 for stalls in privately-operated hawker centres under the Socially Conscious Enterprise Hawker Centre scheme.

sections.label: Hawker centre stall rents
sections.summary: Tender documents show median winning bid for NEA hawker stalls from January to November 2023 was about $1,700, with some over $6,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Good food stalls in NEA-operated hawker centres also face elevated rents, with tender documents revealing that the median winning bid for January to November 2023 was approximately $1,700, with some stalls even fetching over $6,000 in rent, such as the case for the highest-ever $6,810 per month rental for Newton Food Centre hawker stall.

sections.label: Hawkerpreneur costs and earnings
sections.summary: Hawkerpreneurs face higher manpower costs, and a Member asks whether the Ministry studied their average earnings against salary benchmarks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Despite their invaluable contributions, our hawkerpreneurs face escalating challenges, including: one, higher manpower costs, driven by the need to uplift lower-wage workers and the tightness of the labour market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In light of the Government's comprehensive efforts to enhance the livelihoods of lower-wage workers through initiatives like the PWM and increasing local qualifying salaries, it is imperative to consider the well-being and livelihoods of our hawkerpreneurs too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to inquire whether the Ministry has conducted a study on the average earnings of our hawkers, comparing them with the latest salary benchmarks, including overall pay and hourly earning rates?

sections.label: SMU public toilet cleanliness study
sections.summary: An SMU islandwide study found over 66% of 9,411 Singaporeans said hawker centre and coffee shop toilets were as dirty or dirtier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in an islandwide study conducted by SMU last year, more than 66% of 9,411 Singaporeans interviewed were of the view that public toilets in hawker centres and coffee shops either remain as dirty as they were three years ago, or “have become much dirtier”.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: Additionally, about 60% of the respondents also said that efforts in cleaning up toilets in hawker centres and coffee shops ranged from mostly ineffective to completely ineffective; only 6% of Singaporeans were optimistic about the efficacy of clean toilet campaigns.

sections.label: Cleanest public toilets locations
sections.summary: The SMU study found the top three cleanest public toilets in hawker centres and coffee shops in 2023 were in Marina South, Outram and Boon Lay.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in the SMU study, in 2023, the top three cleanest public toilets in hawker centres and coffee shops were those located in Marina South, Outram and Boon Lay.

sections.label: Beefing up surveillance and enforcement
sections.summary: A Member asks whether surveillance and enforcement can be significantly beefed up to deter inconsiderate behaviours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Can I ask if surveillance and the enforcements can be significantly beefed up to deter more of such inconsiderate behaviours?

sections.label: SMU cleanliness survey findings
sections.summary: An SMU survey found over 66% said toilets stayed dirty or worsened, 90% credited cleaning services, and 77% saw cleanliness as Government's responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: According to a study conducted by SMU, also quoted by other Members, more than 66% of Singaporeans said public toilets in hawker centres and coffee shops either remain as dirty as they were three years ago or "have become much dirtier".

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In April 2023, in SMU’s Public Cleanliness Satisfaction Survey, 90% of respondents acknowledged that Singapore is clean only because of the efficiency of its cleaning services and 77% of respondents believe that it is the Government’s responsibility to keep Singapore clean.

sections.label: Orchard Road No Smoking Zone
sections.summary: The Orchard Road No Smoking Zone was expanded to Somerset Skate Park, and MSE will monitor its effectiveness before considering other zones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The Orchard Road "No Smoking Zone" was recently expanded to the Somerset Skate Park.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: In 2021, Minister Grace Fu shared that MSE will monitor and assess the effectiveness of the Orchard Road "No Smoking Zone" before considering whether to designate other areas as "No Smoking Zones".

sections.label: Year of Public Hygiene 2024
sections.summary: MSE will designate 2024 as the Year of Public Hygiene, emphasising environmental services, industry capability and enforcement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: MSE will designate 2024 as the Year of Public Hygiene.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Year of Public Hygiene will see greater emphasis on delivery of public environmental services, resourcing the environmental industry with capability building and technology adoption, and augmenting our enforcement efforts.

sections.label: Environmental Sanitation regime standards
sections.summary: The 2021 Environmental Sanitation regime sets mandatory baseline cleaning and disinfection standards for high-footfall premises with vulnerable occupants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In 2021, we launched the Environmental Sanitation (ES) regime under our Environmental Public Health Act (EPHA) to promote higher cleanliness standards and place greater accountability on businesses to keep their premises clean.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The ES regime sets out mandatory baseline cleaning and disinfection standards for premises with high footfall and vulnerable occupants, such as coffee shops, food courts, schools and eldercare facilities.

sections.label: Cleaners' wage increases
sections.summary: The PWM entails cumulative wage increases of up to 85% from 2022 to 2028, with local cleaners' base salaries rising yearly until 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The PWM also entails a cumulative wage increase of up to 85% from 2022 to 2028, ensuring that our cleaners’ wages continue to rise alongside improvements in their competencies and skillsets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Base salaries of local cleaners have risen to between $1,570 and $2,210 in 2023, and will increase each year until 2028.

sections.label: Licensing exemption for stalls
sections.summary: By 1 January 2025, market stalls and vending machines selling non-food or low-risk food items will not need to be licensed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This helps to reduce regulatory compliance and increase operational efficiency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: I announce that by 1 January 2025, all market stalls and vending machines selling non-food items or low-risk food items, such as canned food and packet biscuits, will not need to be licensed.

sections.label: Formaldehyde interior paint ban
sections.summary: From 2025 onwards, interior paints with formaldehyde will not be allowed for sale in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: From 2025 onwards, interior paints with formaldehyde will not be allowed for sale in Singapore.

sections.label: Cooling tower water sampling rules
sections.summary: The EPHA requires building owners to regularly submit water sampling results to NEA so cooling tower water meets regulatory limits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: As Legionella is primarily spread via inhalation of contaminated water aerosols, the EPHA requires building owners to regularly submit water sampling results to NEA to ensure that the water quality in their cooling towers complies with stipulated regulatory limits.

sections.label: Disposable carrier bag reduction
sections.summary: Since implementation, supermarket operators have observed a 50% to 80% reduction in disposable carrier bag use.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Since its implementation, supermarket operators have observed a 50% to 80% reduction in the use of disposable carrier bags.

sections.label: Cleaner energy cars and grid
sections.summary: About two in three new car registrations in 2023 were cleaner energy cars and one in three HDB carparks have EV charging points.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Thanks to the Ministry of Transport (MOT) and the Land Transport Authority's (LTA’s) efforts, about two in three new car registrations in 2023 were cleaner energy cars, and one in three HDB carparks are now equipped with electrical vehicle charging points.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) and the Energy Market Authority (EMA) are making good progress in greening our national grid, issuing the first Conditional Approvals for low-carbon electricity imports from Cambodia, Indonesia and Vietnam.

sections.label: Singapore emissions peak and net zero
sections.summary: Singapore is committed to peaking emissions before 2030 and achieving net zero by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Singapore is committed to peaking emissions before 2030 and achieving net zero by 2050.

sections.label: Carbon tax rate increases
sections.summary: The carbon tax rate was increased to $25 per tonne this year and will rise to between $50 and $80 per tonne by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As shared by Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean, we have increased the carbon tax rate to $25 per tonne this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will progressively raise it to between $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

sections.label: Energy Efficiency Grant expansion
sections.summary: The Government reviewed existing energy efficiency grants and will subsume the E2F under the expanded Energy Efficiency Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Government has reviewed existing energy efficiency grants by various agencies and will subsume the E2F under the expanded Energy Efficiency Grant (EEG), as announced at Budget 2024.

sections.label: Water heaters and refrigerators standards
sections.summary: From 1 April 2025, labels and standards will be implemented for household water heaters and commercial storage refrigerators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: From 1 April 2025, we will be implementing labels and standards for two more equipment types, namely household water heaters and commercial storage refrigerators.

sections.label: Energy Conservation Act industrial facilities
sections.summary: The Energy Conservation Act will be amended this year for existing industrial facilities from December 2025, with expected savings and cost recovery.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: This has helped new facilities each save an average of $300,000 annually in electricity costs, recouping their initial outlay just after three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will amend the Energy Conservation Act this year to effect similar requirements for existing industrial facilities from December 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Existing industrial facilities can expect average energy savings of about $1.25 million per year per facility across the system's 15-year lifespan and to recover retrofitting and operating costs within five and a half years.

sections.label: Climate Vouchers for HDB households
sections.summary: From 15 April 2024, the CFHP expands to all 1.1 million HDB households, each receiving $300 in Climate Vouchers and more eligible products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As announced by Senior Minister Teo, we will enhance the CFHP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: From 15 April 2024, we will expand the programme to all 1.1 million HDB households in Singapore, a more than three-fold increase in coverage.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Every HDB household will receive $300 worth of Climate Vouchers and the number of eligible product types will be expanded from three to 10, including four-tick washing machines.

sections.label: Climate Vouchers availability and validity
sections.summary: The enhanced Climate Vouchers will be available from 15 April 2024 via RedeemSG and remain valid until 31 December 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The enhanced Climate Vouchers will be available from 15 April 2024 via the RedeemSG platform and remain valid until 31 December 2027.

sections.label: E-waste Extended Producer Responsibility scheme
sections.summary: The e-waste EPR scheme is in its third year, having collected over 16,000 tonnes from over 800 collection points as of December 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: On the e-waste Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) scheme, we are in our third year of implementation and have since collected over 16,000 tonnes of e-waste from over 800 collection points islandwide as of December 2023.

sections.label: Third National Climate Change Study projections
sections.summary: The V3 study showed extreme rainfall is projected to increase and mean sea levels to rise up to 1.15 metres by 2100 and two metres by 2150.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Third National Climate Change Study (V3) by the Centre for Climate Research Singapore released in January this year showed that extreme rainfall is projected to increase, mean sea levels around Singapore are projected to rise higher than previously projected under the V2 study, up to 1.15 metres by 2100 and up to around two metres by 2150.

sections.label: Coastal site-specific studies coverage
sections.summary: With the August 2023 study at Lim Chu Kang and Sungei Kadut, site-specific studies now cover the entire north-west coast from Tuas to Woodlands, Jurong Island and City-East Coast.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: With the commencement of the latest study along the coastlines of Lim Chu Kang and Sungei Kadut in August 2023, our site-specific studies now cover the entire north-west coast from Tuas to Woodlands, as well as Jurong Island and the City-East Coast.

sections.label: Coastal protection legislation plans
sections.summary: To implement coastal protection plans along over 300 kilometres of coastline, coastal protection legislation is being worked towards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To ensure effective implementation of our coastal protection plans along the more than 300 kilometres of our varied coastline, we are working towards enacting coastal protection legislation.

sections.label: 30 by 30 food vision
sections.summary: Global food supply chain volatility drives the aspirational 30 by 30 vision to sustainably produce 30% of nutritional needs locally by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The volatility of global food supply chains underscores the importance of having a buffer, a form of insurance by being able to grow some of our own food locally.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This is the driving force behind our aspirational "30 by 30" vision to build our agri-food industry's capability and capacity to sustainably produce 30% of our nutritional needs locally by 2030.

sections.label: SFA ACT Fund projects
sections.summary: As at the end of last year, SFA committed over S$23 million to fund 60 ACT Fund projects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As at the end of last year, SFA has committed over S$23 million to fund 60 ACT Fund projects.

sections.label: Updated SAP for aquaculture
sections.summary: Principles from a collaborative stakeholder approach will be consolidated in an updated SAP by the second half of this year as a roadmap for aquaculture development.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Lastly, we will also take a collaborative approach with various stakeholders to co-create solutions for sustainability and growth.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: These principles will be consolidated in an updated version of the SAP by the second half of this year and will embody our collective vision and serve as a roadmap for aquaculture development here in Singapore.

sections.label: SAFEF Straits Fish sales
sections.summary: SAFEF plans to sell approximately 50 tonnes of The Straits Fish within six months and develop value-added processed food products for retail and potential export.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: SAFEF now plans to sell approximately 50 tonnes of “The Straits Fish” within the next six months and further develop it into value-added processed food products for sale at retail outlets and potentially for export.

sections.label: FTTRP caterer numbers
sections.summary: As of 1 February 2024, there are 11 FTTRP caterers, up from two previously.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As of 1 February 2024, there are 11 FTTRP caterers, up from two previously.

sections.label: Logo use by farmers
sections.summary: To date, over 100 farmers, distributors and retailers have used the logo on produce packaging and in marketing channels.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To date, over 100 farmers, distributors and retailers have used the logo on produce packaging and in marketing channels.

sections.label: New Food Safety and Security Bill
sections.summary: A new Food Safety and Security Bill will strengthen SFA's legislative powers, consolidating food safety and security legislation from eight Acts into one Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To better protect consumers and safeguard Singapore's food supply resilience, we will strengthen SFA’s legislative powers through the introduction of a new Food Safety and Security Bill (FSSB).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: FSSB will consolidate all food safety and security legislation from eight existing Acts into one Act and provide an overarching framework to ensure coherence across the entire food value chain.

sections.label: Median cooked food stall rental
sections.summary: Median rental across non-subsidised cooked food stalls has remained constant at about $1,225 since 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Median rental across non-subsidised cooked food stalls has remained constant at about $1,225 since 2015.

sections.label: New hawker centres design
sections.summary: Three new hawker centres, each with about 40 cooked food stalls and 700 seats, will be connected to amenities and transport nodes and offer affordable food.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The three new hawker centres, each with about 40 cooked food stalls and 700 seats, will be connected to local amenities and transport nodes, ensuring ease of access for residents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: They have also been designed to offer a pleasant dining environment, with spacious, family-friendly and inclusive seating, centralised dishwashing and high ceilings for improved ventilation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Patrons will also, of course, be able to find affordable food options at these new centres.

sections.label: Year of Public Hygiene
sections.summary: Minister Grace Fu announced earlier that MSE will designate 2024 as the Year of Public Hygiene.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Minister Grace Fu announced earlier that MSE will designate 2024 as the Year of Public Hygiene.

sections.label: Enforcement and return rate
sections.summary: Enforcement starting September 2021 cemented new social norms and raised the return rate from 35% to over 90% today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: By commencing enforcement in September 2021, we managed to cement new social norms and increase the return rate from 35% to over 90% today.

sections.label: Anti-littering enforcement blitzes
sections.summary: NEA will increase the frequency and scale of anti-littering enforcement blitzes at hotspots, planning around five times as many blitzes as in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: NEA will increase the frequency and scale of anti-littering enforcement blitzes, targeting hotspots that have higher offence rates and public feedback reports.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: This year, we plan to conduct around five times as many blitzes compared to 2023.

sections.label: CCTV deployment at hotspots
sections.summary: The deployment of CCTVs at hotspots, including HDB estates, will be quadrupled.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Furthermore, we will quadruple the deployment of CCTVs at hotspots, which include HDB estates.

sections.label: Public Toilets Taskforce formation
sections.summary: A Public Toilets Taskforce will be formed to study and recommend solutions to improve public toilet cleanliness, working with people and private sector partners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will continue to collaborate closely with our partners from the people and private sectors to address the problem of dirty public toilets holistically.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will form a Public Toilets Taskforce to study and recommend solutions to improve the cleanliness of public toilets.

sections.label: Taskforce scope of work
sections.summary: The taskforce will examine good public toilet designs, promote responsible use, advocate premises owners' responsibility, and strengthen community partnership for cleanliness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The taskforce will: one, examine measures for adoption of good public toilet designs; two, promote responsible use of public toilets; three, advocate responsibility among premises owners for toilet cleanliness and maintenance; and four, strengthen community partnership to promote cleanliness.

sections.label: Thermal imaging for rat surveillance
sections.summary: The use of thermal imaging cameras for rat surveillance will be trialled.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: First, we will trial the use of thermal imaging cameras for rat surveillance.

sections.label: Littering enforcement at hotspots
sections.summary: Recalcitrant litterers will undergo Corrective Work Order at high-footfall hotspots, and CCTVs there will be quadrupled to catch litterers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will arrange for recalcitrant litterers to undergo CWO at hotspots with high footfall.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will also quadruple the number of CCTVs deployed at these hotspots to catch litterers.

sections.label: Participants in partner activities
sections.summary: Over 70,000 participants took part in more than 300 activities organised by over 160 partners from the people, private and public sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: More than 70,000 participants took part in over 300 activities organised by more than 160 partners from across the people, private and public sectors.

sections.label: Climate Youth Development Programme run
sections.summary: MSE, with the National Climate Change Secretariat and National Youth Council, ran the inaugural Climate Youth Development Programme with 40 youths from July 2023 to January 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Together with National Climate Change Secretariat and National Youth Council, MSE conducted an inaugural run of the Climate Youth Development Programme with 40 youths from July 2023 to January 2024.

sections.label: GreenHacks Youth Panel findings
sections.summary: Youths in the #GreenHacks Youth Panel are targeting to share preliminary findings and recommendations on sustainable consumption in the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We recognise the importance of co-creating policies with our youths, who will be most impacted by climate change.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We have been supporting a group of passionate youths with a keen interest to make a positive impact through their involvement in the #GreenHacks Youth Panel.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The Panel is targeting to share its preliminary findings and recommendations with regard to sustainable consumption in the second half of this year.

sections.label: Formaldehyde interior paint ban
sections.summary: From 2025 onwards, interior paint with formaldehyde will not be allowed for sale in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Earlier, I said that from 2025 onwards, interior paint with formaldehyde will not be allowed for sale in Singapore.

sections.label: Expanded appliance and household scheme
sections.summary: The scheme is expanded from three to 10 products, to all HDB households, and the $300 is not assigned to fixed products.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: What we have done now is to expand this from three to 10 products.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, a wider variety of household appliances and fittings, including 5-tick air condition, as well as a direct current fan and so on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We are expanding it to beyond the 1- to 3-room-HDB households to all HDB households, as well as the fact that, now, the $300 is not assigned to fixed products.

sections.label: Toilet cleanliness taskforce
sections.summary: A taskforce will look at toilets in coffee shops and hawker centres, which surveys found to be consistently at a very low level of cleanliness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: In fact, based on surveys, the public does find that, for example, toilets at public transport nodes and shopping malls, especially at Changi Airport, these are places where we actually have very high standards of cleanliness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: This taskforce will look at, specifically, toilets in coffee shops and hawker centres which have been found through surveys to be consistently at a very low level and, in fact, some find it even dirtier than before.

sections.label: Cremated ashes public engagement
sections.summary: MSE hopes for steady growth and agrees better awareness and public engagement will raise acceptance of managing cremated ashes, with possible scaling up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: And whether MSE will channel some resources, or more resources to accelerating public conversations to ensure that the take-up rate will be at an accelerated rate?

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We hope that there will be steady growth, and, indeed, we agree with Ms Carrie Tan that better awareness, public engagement will be useful to raise people's acceptance of this method of managing cremated ashes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: I am very happy to work with Ms Carrie Tan if she would like to hold such conversations with residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: And from the experience, we can see how we can scale up in areas, so that people can look at this alternative option.

sections.label: Withdrawal of amendment
sections.summary: The speaker asks leave to withdraw his amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: With that, Sir, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
